correctness.rationale: For fixed 0<r<1 the weight-conjugation gives D(I−sqrt(r)S)^(-1) exactly; the Neumann factor is bounded and D is compact. In the frozen finite-band proof, head rows contribute at most δ/λ to the counting error and tail rows perturb the threshold by λ times O(1/M). The first and last retained block boundaries as well as internal boundaries have only bounded-rank coupling, since the polynomial has fixed bandwidth. Entrywise removal of those couplings leaves independent blocks. Multiplication by the restricted D sandwiches each block singular value between its two endpoint scalings; the Toeplitz-to-circulant replacement has bounded rank. The Fourier grid distribution therefore gives upper/lower Darboux sums for the symbol's level distribution. One-sided envelopes suffice at jumps (including a constant-modulus symbol). Sending mesh size and head cutoff to zero and tail cutoff to infinity gives the layer-cake coefficient. Polynomial truncation at B has error singular values at most t^(B+1)/[(1−t)n] for t=sqrt(r), by the ideal inequality; the count inequalities with thresholds (1±γ)λ give the claimed limit as truncation and γ are taken to zero. Count inversion and harmonic summation give the exact Schatten and Dixmier trace statements. The constant is strictly greater than 1 because the analytic symbol has mean 1 and nonconstant phase. For nonzero eigenvalues, the first nonzero coordinate forces λ=1/m; writing y=(I−tS)^(-1)x produces y_n proportional to binom(n,m)t^(n−m) for n≥m and zero earlier, an ℓ² eigenvector after applying I−tS. The first m rows exclude a generalized vector solving (A−λ)z=x for that eigenvector, so the eigenvalues are simple. evidence: Ponge's Theorem 6.4 explicitly applies to every order −d classical pseudodifferential operator P on a closed d-dimensional manifold; Eq. (6.2) gives lim j μ_j(P) as (2π)^(-d)/d times the cosphere integral of the absolute principal symbol, and gives strong measurability of |P|. Eq. (1.7) states the general singular-value law without selfadjointness.

P_+ is a classical order-zero Fourier multiplier with principal symbol 1 on the positive cotangent ray and 0 on the negative ray. D_+ is classical of order −1: its smooth frequency extension is (ξ+1)^(-1) for ξ≥0 and zero for ξ≤−1/2, smoothly interpolated, and has leading term ξ^(-1) on the positive ray. Consequently B is classical of order −1 on the closed circle, without ellipticity or positivity being required for the singular-value law.
Widom's inspected result is for empirical distributions of finite Toeplitz sections, not the infinite compact product.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The relevant general theorem is the negative-order pseudodifferential Weyl law, not the finite-section Toeplitz distribution, Hilbert–Schmidt formula or compactness criterion. The theorem covers symbols zero on an entire cotangent sheet, so the one-sided Fourier projection is no obstruction.

evidence: The principal symbol of B on S* S¹ is f(θ) at ξ=+1 and zero at ξ=−1. For d=1 the Weyl coefficient is exactly (2π)^(-1)·∫_0^(2π)|f(θ)|dθ, with no extra factor of two. This is the frozen coefficient at t=sqrt(r). Applying the order −d theorem also gives measurability of |B|.

The exact Schatten cutoff and ordinary logarithmic limit follow by comparing the same singular values to the harmonic sequence; c>1 follows from the mean-one symbol with nonconstant phase. The 1984 Rhaly theorem only gives a Hilbert–Schmidt formula, and the 2015 weighted-space corollary includes geometric weights as a compact case, not an individual singular-value formula.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The general Weyl theorem gives precisely the claimed sharp constant after the explicit Fourier identification, and all its featured ideal and trace conclusions follow. The frozen result includes no additional quantitative or structural theorem that escapes this implication.

evidence: The weighted operator is unitarily D(I−tS)^(-1), t=sqrt(r), the geometric generalized Cesàro matrix. On the Hardy subspace of L² of the circle, with basis e^(ikθ), k≥0, this is diagonal multiplication of Fourier coefficients by 1/(k+1) after multiplication by f(θ)=(1−t e^(iθ))^(-1).

Write P_+ for the projection onto modes k≥0 and D_+ for the multiplier (k+1)^(-1) there and zero otherwise. The zero extension of the Hardy-space operator to the full circle is B=D_+ M_f P_+. Its nonzero singular values are exactly the original ones.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The Hardy representation is exact because the smooth analytic symbol f has only nonnegative Fourier modes. The zero extension enables use of the closed-manifold theorem on the full circle without assuming a separate Hardy-space Weyl theorem.
